claims.head: Rovers on the blue line vs. Stay-at-homes
claims.body: The Oilers’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much. Edmonton is near the top of the league for shots from defensemen, and Minnesota is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Oilers’ defensemen jump into the play.

chips.tip: Edmonton: 37% of shot attempts from defensemen, 6th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 9 and 8 games this season.
Minnesota: 31% of shot attempts from defensemen, 32nd of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 9 and 8 games this season.

claims.head: The Oilers’ edge in physicality
claims.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for physicality, and the Wild are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

notes.text: Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 58% of the team’s power-play time in 8 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, down from 30% last season.

stakes: The Wild go in second in the Central with 13 points, the Oilers second in the Pacific with 13 points.

EDM.head: Leaning the Oilers’ way
EDM.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Edmonton has home-ice advantage. The Wild can still swing it if their power play gets going.

MIN.head: A slightly uphill night for the Wild
MIN.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Edmonton has home-ice advantage. The Wild’s best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

items.text: The Wild have been without Marcus Foligno and Jared Spurgeon for several games, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start. Counting how much each missing player usually brings, only the Sabres are missing more right now.
The Oilers have been without Frederik Andersen for several games, and have had to make do without Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Matt Savoie all season. Devon Levi is expected to start.
Matt Boldy has seven goals in eight games against Edmonton since 2023-24.
With Jason Dickinson out, Colton Dach took twelve faceoffs in the Oilers’ last game. He had been taking about two a game.
